plans.note: No liability heading surfaces in the outline; scan the body under the main agreement block for any cap, consequential-damages waiver or disclaimer. Check mutuality and carve-outs (IP infringement, confidentiality, gross negligence) before concluding it is missing.

Look in the general body for an HDI indemnity covering third-party IP claims arising from the site build/hosting, and for any reciprocal indemnity we owe on Deerskin Products content. Treat as missing only if neither direction appears.
Presence rule: nothing in the outline suggests a restraint on the Company's businesses or products. Still sweep the body for any covenant limiting where Deerskin Products may be sold or developed.

A site development and hosting arrangement often makes HDI the sole developer/host for the Deerskin site; check the body and the access provision for words like "sole", "exclusive" or "shall not engage others".
No pricing or favoured-terms heading in the outline. Only flag if the body obliges the Company to extend HDI its best terms; an MFN running in our favour is fine.
Nothing indicates a hiring restriction; the closest is the mutual relationship-manager appointment in 5.4, which is not a non-solicit. Confirm no personnel covenant sits in the body.

"Termination Date" is a defined term, so a term/termination provision exists in the body. Check whether the Company may terminate on notice without penalty and whether HDI has a symmetrical or broader walk-away right.
Review the term language around the defined Termination Date for auto-renewal, the non-renewal notice window and any renewal price uplift.
Boilerplate governing law/venue should sit in the closing body text before the signature block; verify the chosen state and that disputes go to courts rather than arbitration.
Check the boilerplate for assignment and successors language, particularly whether the Company may assign to affiliates/successors and whether HDI gains a termination right on our change of control.

Section 1.4 grants the Company access to something HDI holds (likely site/customer data) — read it for ownership of the developed site, Deerskin Products content and customer data, and for any assignment of our marks or data to HDI.
Treat 1.4 as the primary access/licence grant; test scope for affiliates and contractors, revocability and whether it survives to the Termination Date.

No audit heading appears. Any inspection language would more likely be a Company right over HDI's records (which benefits us and should not be flagged); only an HDI audit of our usage engages this rule.
Direction rule: check fee and termination text for any stipulated damages, early-termination fee or penalty payable by the Company; credits running to us are welcome and not flagged.
Look for HDI warranties on development quality, hosting availability and service levels in the body, together with the remedy and its duration; note any bare disclaimer as a deviation candidate.
No insurance heading in the outline even though HDI hosts our site and handles customer data; confirm absence across the body before recording as missing.
Check the fees/compensation text for guaranteed minimum volumes, minimum hosting fees or take-or-pay language binding the Company; absent an exit right this would be a deviation.
Read the consequences-of-termination text around the Termination Date together with the 1.4 access right for return of customer/site data and migration assistance after expiry.
